content.text:
**No — this is not a backend bug.** The API is doing the right thing.

`403` with code `AUTH_003` means: *you are logged in, but this user/role does not have permission for that endpoint*. That is expected authorization enforcement.

### What each call means

| Endpoint | Typical required permission |
|----------|----------------------------|
| `/notifications/unread/count` | Staff notification access (we map this to `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` in the staff portal) |
| `/billing/statistics` | `BILLING_VIEW` (or similar billing permission) |
| `/billing/history` | `BILLING_VIEW` (or similar billing permission) |

If the custom-role user does **not** have those permissions in `/me`, the backend **should** return 403.

### Why you were seeing it

This was mostly a **frontend gap** after custom staff auth:

1. **Notifications** — `StaffLayout` was calling the unread-count API for **every** staff user, even when they had no notification permission.
2. **Billing** — the billings page was calling statistics/history even when the user shouldn’t have billing access.

I’ve updated the frontend to **skip those API calls** unless the user has the matching staff permission.

### When it *would* be a backend issue

Only if:

- `/me` includes `BILLING_VIEW` (or the notification permission), **and**
- the user can open the Billings / Notifications page in the UI, **but**
- those APIs still return 403.

That would mean a **permission mismatch** between what `/me` returns and what the billing/notification endpoints enforce — that would need backend alignment.

### What to check for your test user

1. Open `/auth/me` (or check login response) for that user’s `permissions` array.
2. Confirm whether they have `BILLING_VIEW` and `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`.
3. If they don’t, 403 is correct — assign those permissions in **Admin → Role Management** for that custom role.

If you share the custom role’s permission list from `/me`, I can tell you exactly which staff menu items and APIs they should be able to use.

# Custom Staff Authorization — Frontend Plan & Backend Alignment Guide

Reference for how the TherapyFlow **frontend** handles **tenant custom roles** (e.g. `BILLING_ROLE`, `INTAKE_CLERK`) and what the **backend** must provide so UI and API authorization stay consistent.

**Base URL:** `/api/v1`  
**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` (staff token from tenant staff login)  
**Primary profile endpoint:** `GET /api/v1/auth/me`  
**Staff login:** `POST /api/v1/auth/staff/login` (resolve-tenant flow)

**Related docs:** [Supervisor API](./supervisor-api.md) · [Notifications API](./notifications-api.md)

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Summary](#summary)
2. [Portal architecture](#portal-architecture)
3. [Role classification](#role-classification)
4. [Login & routing flow](#login--routing-flow)
5. [How the frontend reads permissions](#how-the-frontend-reads-permissions)
6. [Staff portal menu → permission mapping](#staff-portal-menu--permission-mapping)
7. [Action-level UI gating (capabilities)](#action-level-ui-gating-capabilities)
8. [API calls the staff portal makes](#api-calls-the-staff-portal-makes)
9. [Backend requirements](#backend-requirements)
10. [Known mismatch: BILLING_ROLE example](#known-mismatch-billing_role-example)
11. [Test matrix](#test-matrix)
12. [Frontend source files](#frontend-source-files)

---

## Summary

We introduced a **separate staff portal** at `/staff/*` for:

- **Supervisor** (`SUPERVISOR`) — existing clinical oversight role; role-based capability blocks
- **Custom tenant roles** — any role name created in Admin → Role Management that is **not** a fixed portal role

Custom-role users:

1. Sign in via **staff login** (`/auth/staff/login`)
2. Are mapped to app role `staff` (not `admin` / `therapist`)
3. Land in the **staff portal** (`/staff/*`), same shell supervisor uses
4. See **only menu items** whose required permissions appear in `/me` `permissions` (or `authorities`)
5. Are **blocked at the route level** from deep-linking to pages they cannot access
6. See `/staff/no-access` if they have **zero** permissions that match any staff menu route

**Fixed roles are unchanged** — they never use permission-filtered custom staff logic:

| API `roles` | Frontend portal | Path prefix |
|-------------|-----------------|-------------|
| `SUPER_ADMIN`, `PLATFORM_SUPER_ADMIN` | Platform owner | `/super-admin/*` |
| `ADMIN` | Tenant admin | `/admin/*` |
| `THERAPIST` | Therapist | `/therapist/*` |
| `CLIENT` | Client (rejected at staff login) | `/user/*` |
| `SUPERVISOR` | Staff (supervisor model) | `/staff/*` |
| **Any other role name** (e.g. `BILLING_ROLE`) | Staff (permission model) | `/staff/*` |

---

## Portal architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    staffLogin[Staff login] --> roleMapper[mapApiRolesToAppRole]
    roleMapper -->|ADMIN| adminPortal["/admin/*"]
    roleMapper -->|THERAPIST| therapistPortal["/therapist/*"]
    roleMapper -->|SUPER_ADMIN| superAdminPortal["/super-admin/*"]
    roleMapper -->|CLIENT| rejectLogin[Reject at staff login]
    roleMapper -->|SUPERVISOR| staffPortal["/staff/*"]
    roleMapper -->|Custom role e.g. BILLING_ROLE| staffPortal
    staffPortal --> authMe["GET /auth/me"]
    authMe --> menu[Build sidebar from permissions]
    authMe --> routeGuard[StaffRouteGuard per page]
    menu -->|no matching routes| noAccess["/staff/no-access"]
    menu -->|has routes| filteredUI[Filtered UI]
```

**Important:** Admin and therapist pages are **not modified** for custom roles. Custom roles always use copied staff pages under `/staff/*` that call the **same REST APIs** as admin (e.g. `/api/v1/billing/history`).

---

## Role classification

### Fixed portal roles (never treated as custom staff)

These API role names map to dedicated portals and **ignore** permission-based staff portal routing:

```
SUPER_ADMIN
PLATFORM_SUPER_ADMIN
ADMIN
THERAPIST
SUPERVISOR
CLIENT
```

### Custom staff roles

A role is **custom staff** when:

- `roles` is non-empty
- `roles` does **not** include `CLIENT`
- `roles` contains **no** fixed portal role from the list above

Examples:

- `BILLING_ROLE` → custom staff → `/staff/*`
- `INTAKE_COORDINATOR` → custom staff → `/staff/*`
- `ADMIN` + `BILLING_ROLE` → still **admin** portal (fixed role wins by priority)

Custom roles are created in **Admin → User Access → Roles** with arbitrary `name` and a permission set from the tenant permission catalog.

---

## Login & routing flow

### Staff login sequence

1. User signs in at `/auth/staff/login` (resolve tenant → `POST /auth/staff/login`)
2. Frontend reads `roles` from login response
3. `mapApiRolesToAppRole(roles)` determines portal:
   - Fixed roles → existing redirect (`/admin/dashboard`, `/therapist/dashboard`, etc.)
   - Custom role → `staff` → staff portal
4. Session stored: `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `role`, `apiRoles`, `permissions` (from login if present)
5. On `/staff/*` layout mount → `GET /auth/me` refetches authoritative `roles`, `permissions`, `authorities`
6. Landing path = **first allowed staff route** in menu order, or `/staff/no-access`

### Landing route order

| Priority | Staff route | Path |
|----------|-------------|------|
| 1 | Clients | `/staff/clients` |
| 2 | Scheduling | `/staff/scheduling` |
| 3 | Billings | `/staff/billings` |
| 4 | Tasks | `/staff/tasks` |
| 5 | Content → Library | `/staff/content/library` |
| 6 | Content → Assessment | `/staff/content/assessment` |
| 7 | Content → Clinical Forms | `/staff/content/clinical-forms` |
| 8 | Content → Process Checklists | `/staff/content/process-checklists` |
| 9 | Compliance → HIPAA | `/staff/compliance/hipaa` |
| 10 | Compliance → Privacy | `/staff/compliance/privacy` |
| 11 | Notifications | `/staff/system/notifications` |

### Zero permissions

If a custom-role user has **no permissions** matching any row in [Staff portal menu → permission mapping](#staff-portal-menu--permission-mapping):

- Login **succeeds**
- User lands on **`/staff/no-access`**
- Sidebar is **empty**
- Topbar/profile still works

---

## How the frontend reads permissions

### Source of truth: `GET /api/v1/auth/me`

Expected shape (relevant fields):

```json
{
  "identityType": "STAFF",
  "roles": ["BILLING_ROLE"],
  "permissions": ["BILLING_VIEW", "BILLING_MANAGE", "..."],
  "authorities": ["BILLING_VIEW", "ROLE_BILLING_ROLE", "..."],
  "isTenantAdmin": false,
  "isSupervisor": false,
  "isTherapist": false,
  "isClient": false
}
```

### Merge rule

```ts
effectivePermissions = me.permissions ?? me.authorities ?? []
```

All menu, route guard, and capability checks use **`effectivePermissions`** (case-insensitive string match).

### Supervisor special case

If `roles` includes `SUPERVISOR` **and** `permissions` is empty:

- Frontend shows the **full staff menu** (legacy supervisor UX)
- Capability blocks still apply (no delete client, no user management, etc.)

Custom roles **never** get the empty-permissions full-menu fallback.

---

## Staff portal menu → permission mapping

This table is what the frontend uses to show/hide sidebar items and guard routes.

| Staff UI module | Route path | Required permission(s) | Rule |
|-----------------|------------|--------------------------|------|
| **Clients** | `/staff/clients` | `CLIENT_VIEW` **or** `CLIENT_VIEW_ALL` **or** `CLIENT_VIEW_OWN` | any |
| **Scheduling** | `/staff/scheduling` | `SESSION_VIEW` **or** `SESSION_EDIT` **or** `SESSION_CREATE` | any |
| **Billings** | `/staff/billings` | `BILLING_VIEW` **or** `BILLING_MANAGE` **or** `BILLING_EDIT` | any |
| **Tasks** | `/staff/tasks` | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | all |
| **Content → Library** | `/staff/content/library` | `USER_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | any |
| **Content → Assessment** | `/staff/content/assessment` | `ASSESSMENT_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | any |
| **Content → Clinical Forms** | `/staff/content/clinical-forms` | `FORM_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | any |
| **Content → Process Checklists** | `/staff/content/process-checklists` | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | all |
| **Compliance → HIPAA** | `/staff/compliance/hipaa` | `AUDIT_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | any |
| **Compliance → Privacy** | `/staff/compliance/privacy` | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | all |
| **Notifications** | `/staff/system/notifications` | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | all |

**Backend implication:** If `/me` includes a permission for a module, the user will see that module and the frontend will call the corresponding APIs. Those APIs **must** allow the same permission (or a documented subset), not only fixed roles like `ADMIN` / `THERAPIST`.

---

## Action-level UI gating (capabilities)

Route access controls **pages**. Capabilities control **buttons/actions** inside pages (for custom staff only).

| UI action | Permission required |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Delete / restore client | `CLIENT_DELETE` |
| Bulk portal access | `CLIENT_EDIT` |
| Manage users | `USER_MANAGE` |
| Manage roles | `ROLE_ADMIN` |
| Notification setup | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |
| Checklist templates / system options / practice config | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |
| Library tags | `USER_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |
| Billing mutations (pay, discount, status) | `BILLING_MANAGE` **or** `BILLING_EDIT` |
| Edit client | `CLIENT_EDIT` |

**Supervisor** keeps role-based blocks (e.g. cannot delete client) regardless of permissions.

---

## API calls the staff portal makes

Staff pages reuse **admin API modules**. Custom-role users hit the **same endpoints** as tenant admin, scoped by backend authorization.

### Always considered (staff layout)

| Endpoint | When called | Frontend gate |
|----------|-------------|---------------|
| `GET /api/v1/auth/me` | Every `/staff/*` session | Always |
| `GET /api/v1/notifications/unread/count` | Staff layout bootstrap | Only if user has `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` (notifications route access) |

### Per visible module (examples)

| Module | Example endpoints | Expected permission (backend should align) |
|--------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| **Billings** | `GET /billing/statistics`, `GET /billing/history`, `POST /billing/billing/{id}/record-payment`, `PATCH .../discount`, `PATCH .../status` | `BILLING_VIEW` (read), `BILLING_MANAGE` / `BILLING_EDIT` (write) |
| **Clients** | `GET /clients`, `GET /clients/{id}`, `PATCH /clients/{id}`, portal access endpoints | `CLIENT_VIEW*` (read), `CLIENT_EDIT` (update), `CLIENT_DELETE` (delete) |
| **Scheduling** | Session list/create/edit APIs | `SESSION_VIEW`, `SESSION_CREATE`, `SESSION_EDIT` |
| **Tasks** | Task APIs | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` (current frontend mapping) |
| **Content / Assessment** | Assessment APIs | `ASSESSMENT_VIEW` |
| **Content / Clinical Forms** | Form template APIs | `FORM_VIEW` |
| **Compliance / HIPAA** | Audit APIs | `AUDIT_VIEW` |
| **Notifications** | `GET /notifications`, unread count, etc. | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |

**Contract:** For every row in the [menu mapping table](#staff-portal-menu--permission-mapping), if `/me` grants the permission, the backend endpoints for that module should return **200** (or appropriate data), not **403 AUTH_003**.

---

## Backend requirements

### 1. `/auth/me` must be authoritative

- `permissions` and `authorities` must reflect the **effective** grants for custom roles
- Custom role names (e.g. `BILLING_ROLE`) appear in `roles`
- Flags (`isTenantAdmin`, `isSupervisor`, etc.) should remain accurate

### 2. API security must use **permissions**, not only fixed roles

Today we observe:

- `/me` returns billing permissions for `BILLING_ROLE`
- `/billing/statistics` and `/billing/history` return **403 AUTH_003** for the same JWT

This indicates endpoint guards likely check **role names** (`ADMIN`, `THERAPIST`, `SUPERVISOR`) but not **authorities** (`BILLING_VIEW`, etc.).

**Required fix pattern:**

```text
Allow if authenticated staff AND (
  hasAuthority('BILLING_VIEW')   -- for GET statistics/history
  OR hasAuthority('BILLING_MANAGE')
  OR hasRole('ADMIN')            -- optional: keep fixed roles working
  ...
)
```

Apply the same pattern across all modules in the menu mapping table.

### 3. Custom roles use the same APIs as admin

The frontend does **not** call separate `/staff/billing/*` routes. Custom staff with `BILLING_VIEW` calls:

- `GET /api/v1/billing/statistics`
- `GET /api/v1/billing/history`

Backend must authorize custom roles on these paths.

### 4. JWT / security context

Ensure custom role authorities from tenant RBAC are loaded into the Spring Security context (or equivalent) for every request, not only serialized in `/me`.

Typical expected authorities for `BILLING_ROLE`:

```json
[
  "BILLING_VIEW",
  "BILLING_MANAGE",
  "BILLING_CREATE",
  "BILLING_EDIT",
  "BILLING_DELETE",
  "BILLING_EXPORT",
  "ROLE_BILLING_ROLE"
]
```

`ROLE_*` prefixes are fine; frontend checks the `BILLING_*` permission strings.

### 5. Data scope (optional but recommended)

Document per permission whether access is:

- **Org-wide** (like admin)
- **Own/team only** (like therapist)

Frontend currently does not enforce data scope; backend should enforce row-level scope consistently for custom roles.

---

## Known mismatch: BILLING_ROLE example

**Test user:** `biller.north`  
**Role:** `BILLING_ROLE`  
**Tenant:** `tenant_northstar`

### `/me` (200 OK) — correct

```json
{
  "roles": ["BILLING_ROLE"],
  "permissions": [
    "BILLING_MANAGE",
    "BILLING_VIEW",
    "BILLING_CREATE",
    "BILLING_DELETE",
    "BILLING_EXPORT",
    "BILLING_EDIT"
  ],
  "authorities": [
    "BILLING_MANAGE",
    "BILLING_VIEW",
    "BILLING_CREATE",
    "BILLING_DELETE",
    "ROLE_BILLING_ROLE",
    "BILLING_EXPORT",
    "BILLING_EDIT"
  ]
}
```

### Frontend behavior — correct

- Maps to staff portal
- Shows **Billings** menu only
- Lands on `/staff/billings`
- Calls billing statistics + history APIs

### API behavior — **incorrect today**

| Endpoint | Status | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `GET /billing/statistics` | **403 AUTH_003** | Should allow with `BILLING_VIEW` |
| `GET /billing/history` | **403 AUTH_003** | Should allow with `BILLING_VIEW` |
| `GET /notifications/unread/count` | **403 AUTH_003** | Expected — user has no `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`; frontend now skips this call |

**Backend action item:** Update billing module authorization so custom roles with `BILLING_VIEW` / `BILLING_MANAGE` can access billing read/write endpoints.

---

## Test matrix

| User type | `roles` | Expected portal | Menu source |
|-----------|---------|-----------------|-------------|
| Tenant admin | `["ADMIN"]` | `/admin/*` | Full admin menu |
| Therapist | `["THERAPIST"]` | `/therapist/*` | Full therapist menu |
| Platform owner | `["SUPER_ADMIN"]` | `/super-admin/*` | Super-admin menu |
| Supervisor | `["SUPERVISOR"]` | `/staff/*` | Full staff menu if permissions empty; else filtered |
| Billing clerk | `["BILLING_ROLE"]` + `BILLING_VIEW` | `/staff/*` | Billings only |
| Custom role, clients only | `["CUSTOM"]` + `CLIENT_VIEW` | `/staff/*` | Clients only |
| Custom role, no permissions | `["CUSTOM"]` + `[]` | `/staff/no-access` | Empty menu |
| Client on staff login | `["CLIENT"]` | Login error | N/A |

### Backend verification checklist per custom role

For each permission assigned to a custom role in Role Management:

1. `GET /auth/me` includes that permission in `permissions` or `authorities`
2. Every API endpoint used by the matching staff UI module accepts that permission
3. No **403 AUTH_003** when permission is present (unless data scope intentionally denies a specific row)
4. Fixed-role users (`ADMIN`, `THERAPIST`, `SUPERVISOR`) still work as before

---

## Frontend source files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/utils/roleMapper.ts` | Fixed vs custom role → app portal role |
| `src/utils/staffPermissions.ts` | Menu/route/capability permission maps |
| `src/utils/staffMenu.tsx` | Sidebar builder |
| `src/hooks/useStaffPermissionsBootstrap.ts` | Loads `/me` into Redux |
| `src/hooks/useStaffAccess.ts` | Permission/capability hook for pages |
| `src/components/staff/StaffRouteGuard.tsx` | Route-level access control |
| `src/pages/staff/no-access/index.tsx` | Zero-access state |
| `src/layouts/StaffLayout.tsx` | Staff portal shell |
| `src/pages/auth/therapist/login/index.tsx` | Staff login + redirect |

---

## Backend ticket template

Copy/paste for issue tracking:

```text
Title: Align API authorization with custom tenant roles (staff portal)

Context:
The frontend staff portal (/staff/*) supports tenant custom roles (e.g. BILLING_ROLE).
Users sign in via staff login; UI visibility is driven by GET /auth/me permissions.

Problem:
/me returns permissions for custom roles, but some module APIs return 403 AUTH_003
for the same JWT. Example: BILLING_ROLE with BILLING_VIEW cannot call
GET /billing/statistics or GET /billing/history.

Required:
- Authorize endpoints by permission authorities (BILLING_VIEW, CLIENT_VIEW, etc.),
  not only fixed roles (ADMIN, THERAPIST, SUPERVISOR).
- Ensure JWT security context includes custom role authorities on every request.
- See docs/custom-staff-authorization.md for full menu → permission → API mapping.
```

content.text:
**Why Content → Library was showing**

It was a **frontend mapping mistake**, not because `biller.north` has a library permission.

The staff menu mapped **Library** like this:

```ts
"content-library": { anyPermission: ["USER_VIEW", "CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW"] }
```

`biller.north` has **`USER_VIEW`** (and `USER_MANAGE`) because those are required for **session scheduling** (pick therapists/rooms) — not for the clinical library.

So Library appeared even though this user has **no** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`, `ASSESSMENT_VIEW`, `FORM_VIEW`, etc.

### Your permissions vs Content menu

| Permission you have | What it unlocks in staff portal |
|---------------------|----------------------------------|
| `CLIENT_*` | Clients |
| `SESSION_*` | Scheduling |
| `BILLING_*` | Billings |
| `USER_VIEW`, `USER_MANAGE`, `ROOM_MANAGE` | Used for scheduling/user/room APIs — **not** Content |
| `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` | Tasks, notifications, **Library**, checklists, etc. — **you don't have this** |

There is **no separate `LIBRARY_VIEW`** permission in your `/me` response. Library was incorrectly tied to `USER_VIEW`.

### Fix applied

Library now requires **`CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` only**:

```ts
"content-library": { permissions: ["CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW"] }
```

After refresh, `biller.north` should **no longer** see Content → Library. They should only see **Clients**, **Scheduling**, and **Billings** based on their current permissions.

| `USER_EDIT` or `USER_MANAGE` | Edit basic info, professional details, activate/deactivate |

Role Management and Duplicate Detection are **not** exposed in staff — those stay admin-only.

content.text:
Cross-checked the staff portal against your permission spec and aligned the frontend. Summary:

## Core rule
- `/me` bootstrap already merges `permissions ?? authorities` into Redux (`useStaffPermissionsBootstrap`).
- Custom staff actions use `useStaffAccess().can()` / `hasAny()` from that set — not `isTenantAdmin` or `roles.includes('ADMIN')`.
- Fixed portal users (`ADMIN`, `THERAPIST`, `SUPERVISOR`) keep their existing portals; custom roles stay on `/staff/*`.

## Route / menu fixes (were wrong)

| Route | Was | Now |
|-------|-----|-----|
| Clients | Missing `CLIENT_VIEW_TEAM` | Added |
| Scheduling | Missing `SESSION_VIEW` | `SESSION_VIEW` \| `SESSION_CREATE` \| `SESSION_EDIT` |
| Library | `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` only | `USER_VIEW` \| `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |
| Assessment | Missing `ASSESSMENT_ASSIGN` | `ASSESSMENT_VIEW` \| `ASSESSMENT_ASSIGN` \| `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |

## Capability / action fixes

| Area | Fix |
|------|-----|
| **Bulk portal access** | Was incorrectly requiring `CLIENT_DELETE` for supervisors; now `CLIENT_EDIT` |
| **Billing mutations** | `paySubscriptionInvoice` now allows `BILLING_EDIT` **or** `BILLING_MANAGE` |
| **Library tags** | `manageLibraryTags` → `USER_VIEW` **or** `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` |
| **Library writes** | Staff library read-only unless `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW` (add/edit/delete/bulk hidden) |
| **Custom staff clients** | Edit/portal gated by `CLIENT_EDIT` only (no supervisor override for custom roles) |
| **Custom staff billing** | Mutations gated by `BILLING_EDIT`/`BILLING_MANAGE` only (no supervisor override) |
| **Scheduling** | New Session → `SESSION_CREATE`; edits → `SESSION_EDIT` |

## Assessments (new split)
Added helpers in `staffPermissions.ts`:
- `canViewAssessments()` → `ASSESSMENT_VIEW` \| `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`
- `canAssignAssessments()` → `ASSESSMENT_ASSIGN` \| `CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`

Staff assessment page now uses permission-based `assessmentAccess` instead of blanket `staffMode`:
- **View only** (`ASSESSMENT_VIEW`): list + read templates/assignments
- **Assign** (`ASSESSMENT_ASSIGN`): assign, status changes, template CRUD
- **Admin proxy** (`CONSENT_ADMIN_VIEW`): full UI

## Helpers added
```ts
buildStaffPermissionSet(permissions)
staffHasAny(permissions, ...keys)
useStaffAccess().hasAny(...keys)
```

## Still intentional
- **Supervisor** (`SUPERVISOR` role): keeps legacy role-based blocks (e.g. no delete client) when not a custom staff role.
- **User Management** on staff: not in your module table but wired for `USER_*` permissions; supervisor tab and status column remain hidden on staff.
- **`CLIENT_EXPORT`**: documented; no export button found on staff clients page yet (add when export UI exists).

`docs/custom-staff-authorization.md` is updated to match this model. Build passes.

Yes — **admin, therapist, supervisor, and super-admin are unchanged in behavior.**

Here's why:

### Fixed roles keep their own portals
- `ADMIN` → `/admin/*`
- `THERAPIST` → `/therapist/*`
- `SUPERVISOR` → `/staff/*` with the **existing** supervisor rules (full menu when permissions aren't loaded, role-based blocks like no delete client)
- Custom roles (`BILLING_ROLE`, etc.) → `/staff/*` with **permission-based** UI

Route guards and menu filtering only apply when `role === "staff"` **and** the user is a custom staff role. Admin/therapist routes don't go through `StaffRouteGuard`.

### Shared components use safe defaults for admin
Where admin reuses the same components, defaults preserve full access:

| Component | Admin behavior |
|-----------|----------------|
| `AdminAssessment` | No `assessmentAccess` prop → all actions enabled (same as before) |
| `AdminLibrary` | `canWriteEntries` defaults to `true` |
| `UserProfiles` / `UserProfileTable` | No `userAccess` prop → all tabs/actions enabled |
| `SupervisorAssignmentTable` | `canManageAssignments` defaults to `true` |

### Staff-only code paths
These only run on `/staff/*` for custom roles:
- `useStaffAccess()` / `useStaffPortalRestrictions()`
- `getStaffUserAccessPermissions()` (hides supervisor tab, status column on staff)
- `buildStaffMenuItems()` permission filtering
- Staff page wrappers (`StaffLibrary`, `StaffAssessment`, `StaffUserProfiles`, etc.)

### What did **not** change
- Admin routes in `routes/index.tsx`
- Therapist routes and pages
- Login / role mapping for fixed roles
- Admin sidebar (`menuList.tsx`)
- Admin clients, billing, scheduling pages directly

So a tenant **admin** logging into `/admin` sees the same UI and capabilities as before. The permission gating only affects **custom staff** users on `/staff/*`.

[REDACTED]

<user_query>
but you made changes in the admin/ files what are they for?
</user_query>

The `admin/` edits are there so **staff can reuse the same screens** without copying them. Admin behavior stays the same because every change is **opt-in via optional props with admin-friendly defaults**.

### Why touch admin files at all?

Staff User Management, Library, and Assessment don’t have separate implementations — they render the admin components:

- `/staff/user-access/profiles` → `UserProfiles` (admin)
- `/staff/content/library` → `AdminLibrary`
- `/staff/content/assessment` → `AdminAssessment`

So permission gating had to live in those shared components (or we’d duplicate large tables/pages).

### What changed in each admin file

| File | Change | Admin impact |
|------|--------|--------------|
| `pages/admin/user-access/profiles/index.tsx` | Optional `userAccess` prop | Admin route uses no prop → **full access** (both tabs, all buttons) |
| `components/access-profile-sections/UserProfileTable.tsx` | Hide status/actions based on `userAccess` | Admin default = show everything |
| `components/access-profile-sections/SupervisorAssignmentTable.tsx` | Optional `canManageAssignments` | Admin default = `true` |
| `pages/admin/content/assessment/index.tsx` | Optional `assessmentAccess` (replaces blunt `staffMode`) | Admin default = create/assign/edit/delete all enabled |
| `pages/admin/content/library/index.tsx` | Optional `canWriteEntries` | Admin default = `true` (add/edit/delete visible) |
| `components/admin-library-sections/LibraryEntryCard.tsx` | `onSelect` / edit / delete optional | Admin still passes all handlers |

### Pattern

```tsx
// Admin — unchanged usage
<UserProfiles />
<AdminLibrary />
<AdminAssessment />

// Staff — same components, restricted props
<UserProfiles userAccess={getStaffUserAccessPermissions(permissions)} />
<AdminLibrary canWriteEntries={false} />
<AdminAssessment assessmentAccess={{ canView: true, canAssign: false, ... }} />
```

### Bottom line

- **Admin routes** (`/admin/*`) were not rewired and don’t pass restriction props.
- **Defaults** match the old behavior (everything on).
- Only **staff wrappers** pass the limited permissions.

If you prefer zero edits under `admin/`, the alternative is to fork those pages into `pages/staff/...` — more duplication, but admin files stay untouched. The current approach is shared UI with permission props on the staff side only.

Investigating how the clinical forms edit flow maps API template data, especially `activeVersion.instructions`.

[REDACTED]

The API stores instructions on `activeVersion`, but the UI reads the top-level field (null). Updating normalization to prefer `activeVersion` when top-level values are missing.

[REDACTED]

**What was happening**

The API returns template metadata in two places:

| Field | Top-level | `activeVersion` (v2, ACTIVE) |
|-------|-----------|-------------------------------|
| `instructions` | `null` | `"without testing do not submit it"` |
| `description` | `"testing to the client"` | same |
| `fields` | `null` | `null` (in sections too) |

The UI should use the **active version** when the top-level value is missing. It was only reading top-level `instructions`, so the edit modal showed an empty Instructions field.

It was **not** copying from an old archived version — it was simply ignoring `activeVersion.instructions`.

---

**Fix applied**

Updated `normalizeAdminFormTemplate` in `clients.api.ts` so when loading a template by ID it resolves:

- `instructions` → top-level, else `activeVersion.instructions`
- `description` → top-level, else `activeVersion.description`
- `name` → top-level, else `activeVersion.name`
- `fields` → top-level, else `activeVersion.fields`

Edit template, consent builder, and save flows all use this normalized data.

---

content.text:
Two fixes on the create-assessment page:

### 1. Error toast color
The page was using `isFetchError` to pick toast color, so save errors (e.g. 400) showed green. It now uses the shared `Toast` component with an explicit `toastType` — **success = green**, **error = red**.

### 2. UI out of sync after delete + save
Two causes:
- **Local state drift:** If you deleted a section and save failed (e.g. active assignments), the UI stayed empty while the server still had the section.
- **Missing IDs in payload:** Existing sections/questions weren’t sent with their server IDs, so the backend couldn’t reconcile deletions.

**Fixes:**
- Include persisted `id` values on sections, questions, and options when saving.
- After **any** save attempt (success or failure), refetch from the server and reset the UI to match what’s actually stored.

So if save fails with *"Cannot update template with active assignments..."*, you’ll see a **red** error toast and the deleted section will reappear in the UI to match the API. If save succeeds, deletions should persist correctly.

### What was wrong
1. **Active `gh` account was `Fahad-Jameel`** — invalid token and suspended, so Git operations failed.

### What I fixed
1. Switched active account: `gh auth switch -u MachineIntelligence6`
2. Re-synced Git with `gh`: `gh auth setup-git`
3. Cleared old cached credentials (git credential + Keychain entry for `github.com`)

### Result
`git push` works now. Your commit was pushed successfully:

```
main -> main (afff9bf)
```

---

**If you want to push as `Fahad-Jameel` (collaborator account) instead:**

That account still shows as suspended/invalid in `gh`. You’ll need to:

```bash
gh auth login -h github.com   # log in as Fahad-Jameel with a fresh token
gh auth switch -u Fahad-Jameel
gh auth setup-git
```

Then push again. If GitHub still says the account is suspended, that has to be resolved in GitHub support — credentials alone won’t fix that.

**Going forward:** After switching accounts with `gh auth switch`, always run `gh auth setup-git` so `git push` uses the same token as `gh`.
